title: Four ring operations for one constant-ring comparison
statement: Let (C,JC),(D,JD) be small sites, L a finite-limit-preserving functor of set-sheaf categories, and κ:constant_C ⋙ L ≅ constant_D an isomorphism natural in all sets [lem-route-inverse-image-constant-set-comparison]. Assume commutative-ring sheafification exists. Let A be any commutative ring, RI a commutative-ring sheaf on D, and e:L(|constant_C A|)≅|RI| compatible with the generalized-section graphs of addition, multiplication, zero and one (the record CategoryTheory.RingInverseImage, extracted unchanged from the parent module). Write κ_A^ring for the conjugation by constantCommuteCompose. Then for every U∈D, the function f_U=(e^{-1};κ_A^ring)_U:RI(U)→(constant_D A)(U) preserves zero, one, addition and multiplication. This is only a pointwise operation statement for one A; it asserts neither a ring-sheaf isomorphism nor naturality in A.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: Identify the underlying constant ring sheaf with the constant set sheaf by constantCommuteCompose. Define constantMap by applying the constant-set functor to any function into A and then the inverse comparison. Naturality of the sheafification unit and sheafComposeIso_hom_fac identify this map on unit sections. The map coeffPair induced by the two projections A×A→A is an isomorphism: factor it through the Types binary-product isomorphism, the product comparison for the constant-set functor, and the product of the underlying-set comparison isomorphisms. Set sheafification preserves finite products.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: Define addMap and mulMap pointwise for two maps of set sheaves into a ring sheaf. Their naturality is the preservation of operations by the restriction ring homomorphisms. The constant map of the sum, respectively product, of two functions equals addMap, respectively mulMap, of their constant maps. Prove these morphism identities by sheafify_hom_ext, checking the unit sections with the preceding unit equation and the ring-homomorphism properties of the ring-valued sheafification unit.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: Naturality of κ for every function g:X→A gives L(constantMap_C(g));κ_A^ring = κ_X;constantMap_D(g), by cancelling the source underlying-set comparison with its inverse. The morphism L(coeffPair);prodComparison(L);(e×e) is an isomorphism from L of the constant pair sheaf to |RI|×|RI|. Evaluating its inverse on the sectionwise pair (x,y) provides a test section p whose two projections are x and y. Apply e.ringAdd or e.ringMul to the constant maps of the two projections and the corresponding operation, using the source identities from step 2. Compose with f=e⁻¹;κ_A^ring, cancel e;e⁻¹, and use the naturality equations and target identity from step 2. This gives f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y) and f(xy)=f(x)f(y).

source.place: Tag 0H7J (Example example-constant-sheaf) and Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): constant sheaves and inverse image of algebraic structures

proof.text: Use the endomorphism z of the source underlying constant ring sheaf that is identically one. The normalization of the canonical comparison on constant sections implies κ_A^ring(L(z)(p))=1 for every p. Apply e.ringOne and evaluate at p=e⁻¹(1). Since e is injective and e(L(z)(p))=1=e(p), obtain L(z)(p)=p, hence f(1)=1. Finally the additive identity at (0,0), followed by cancellation in the target additive group, gives f(0)=0. This uses neither a nonzero ring nor a nonempty-cover assumption.

mathlib_searches.query: A left exact left adjoint between sheaf categories commutes with constant sheaves, naturally in all sets and preserving the ring operations on constant rings
mathlib_searches.results: constantSheafΓAdj and constantCommuteCompose support the construction; no arbitrary inverse-image comparison theorem. A separate ring-operation query returned no ring-operation comparison theorem.

mathlib_searches.results: constantSheafAdj_counit_w and Sheaf.isConstant_of_forget; neither constructs this inverse-image comparison.
constantSheaf, constantCommuteCompose, and IsConstant lemmas; no comparison under an arbitrary geometric adjunction.

lean.statement: theorem constantComparison_ring_operations {C D : Type u} [SmallCategory C] [SmallCategory D] (JC : GrothendieckTopology C) (JD : GrothendieckTopology D) [HasWeakSheafify JC CommRingCat.{u}] [HasWeakSheafify JD CommRingCat.{u}] (L : Sheaf JC (Type u) ⥤ Sheaf JD (Type u)) (hL : PreservesFiniteLimits L) (kappa : constantSheaf JC (Type u) ⋙ L ≅ constantSheaf JD (Type u)) (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (RI : Sheaf JD CommRingCat.{u}) (e : RingInverseImage L ((constantSheaf JC CommRingCat.{u}).obj A) RI) : let f : ∀ U : Dᵒᵖ, RI.obj.obj U → ((constantSheaf JD CommRingCat.{u}).obj A).obj.obj U := fun U x ↦ (e.ringUnderlying.inv ≫ (constantRingSetComparison JC JD L kappa).hom.app A).hom.app U x ∀ U : Dᵒᵖ, f U 0 = 0 ∧ f U 1 = 1 ∧ (∀ x y : RI.obj.obj U, f U (x + y) = f U x + f U y) ∧ (∀ x y : RI.obj.obj U, f U (x * y) = f U x * f U y)
